text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-After a period of heavy rain, Norway's water reservoirs are almost back to normal levels. As a result, electricity prices are expected to fall after Easter.
-Doctors tend to avoid reporting "near accidents" due to fear of being exposed in media. Doctors feel insecure over their legal protection, says Grethe Aasved, head of the young doctors' association.

-European Champions Juventus were held to a 1-1 draw in the first leg of the quarter-finals of the European Cup by Norwegian part-timers Rosenborg Trondheim. The second leg will be held in Italy in two weeks' time.
-Storebrand ASA, Norway's biggest insurance company, posted 1.25 billion crowns in group profits in 1996, 13.6 percent less than in 1995.

-The government will not offer financial support to tempt U.S. microchip producer Atmel to Norway. For over a year SND, a state body for development in the districts, has been trying to get Atmel to set up in Norway.
-The Czech Republic will most propably buy natural gas from Norway. Sources in Prague say the Czech Industry Minister will present the decision next Tuesday.
